nodes.Name: maxExecDepth
nodes.DocComment:
maxExecDepth specifies the maximum stack depth of templates within
templates. This limit is only practically reached by accidentally
recursive template invocations. This limit allows us to return
an error instead of triggering a stack overflow.

nodes.Name: state
nodes.DocComment:
state represents the state of an execution. It's not part of the
template so that multiple executions of the same template
can execute in parallel.

Fields.Name: depth
Fields.DocComment: the height of the stack of executing templates.

nodes.Name: variable
nodes.DocComment: variable holds the dynamic value of a variable such as $, $x etc.

nodes.Name: push
nodes.DocComment: push pushes a new variable on the stack.

nodes.Name: mark
nodes.DocComment: mark returns the length of the variable stack.

nodes.Name: pop
nodes.DocComment: pop pops the variable stack up to the mark.

nodes.Name: setVar
nodes.DocComment:
setVar overwrites the last declared variable with the given name.
Used by variable assignments.

nodes.Name: setTopVar
nodes.DocComment: setTopVar overwrites the top-nth variable on the stack. Used by range iterations.

nodes.Name: varValue
nodes.DocComment: varValue returns the value of the named variable.

nodes.Name: at
nodes.DocComment: at marks the state to be on node n, for error reporting.

nodes.Name: doublePercent
nodes.DocComment:
doublePercent returns the string with %'s replaced by %%, if necessary,
so it can be used safely inside a Printf format string.

nodes.Name: ExecError
nodes.DocComment:
ExecError is the custom error type returned when Execute has an
error evaluating its template. (If a write error occurs, the actual
error is returned; it will not be of type ExecError.)

nodes.Name: errorf
nodes.DocComment: errorf records an ExecError and terminates processing.

nodes.Name: writeError
nodes.DocComment:
writeError is the wrapper type used internally when Execute has an
error writing to its output. We strip the wrapper in errRecover.
Note that this is not an implementation of error, so it cannot escape
from the package as an error value.

nodes.Name: errRecover
nodes.DocComment:
errRecover is the handler that turns panics into returns from the top
level of Parse.

nodes.Name: ExecuteTemplate
nodes.DocComment:
ExecuteTemplate applies the template associated with t that has the given name
to the specified data object and writes the output to wr.
If an error occurs executing the template or writing its output,
execution stops, but partial results may already have been written to
the output writer.
A template may be executed safely in parallel, although if parallel
executions share a Writer the output may be interleaved.

nodes.Name: Execute
nodes.DocComment:
Execute applies a parsed template to the specified data object,
and writes the output to wr.
If an error occurs executing the template or writing its output,
execution stops, but partial results may already have been written to
the output writer.
A template may be executed safely in parallel, although if parallel
executions share a Writer the output may be interleaved.

If data is a [reflect.Value], the template applies to the concrete
value that the reflect.Value holds, as in [fmt.Print].

nodes.Name: DefinedTemplates
nodes.DocComment:
DefinedTemplates returns a string listing the defined templates,
prefixed by the string "; defined templates are: ". If there are none,
it returns the empty string. For generating an error message here
and in [html/template].

nodes.Name: walkBreak
nodes.DocComment: Sentinel errors for use with panic to signal early exits from range loops.

nodes.Name: walkContinue
nodes.DocComment: Sentinel errors for use with panic to signal early exits from range loops.

nodes.Name: walk
nodes.DocComment:
Walk functions step through the major pieces of the template structure,
generating output as they go.

nodes.Name: walkIfOrWith
nodes.DocComment:
walkIfOrWith walks an 'if' or 'with' node. The two control structures
are identical in behavior except that 'with' sets dot.

nodes.Name: IsTrue
nodes.DocComment:
IsTrue reports whether the value is 'true', in the sense of not the zero of its type,
and whether the value has a meaningful truth value. This is the definition of
truth used by if and other such actions.

Children.Name: case
Children.RawSource: reflect.Uint, reflect.Uint8, reflect.Uint16, reflect.Uint32, reflect.Uint64, reflect.Uintptr

Children.Name: case
Children.RawSource: reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64, reflect.Uint, reflect.Uint8, reflect.Uint16, reflect.Uint32, reflect.Uint64, reflect.Uintptr

nodes.Name: evalPipeline
nodes.DocComment:
evalPipeline returns the value acquired by evaluating a pipeline. If the
pipeline has a variable declaration, the variable will be pushed on the
stack. Callers should therefore pop the stack after they are finished
executing commands depending on the pipeline value.

nodes.Name: idealConstant
nodes.DocComment:
idealConstant is called to return the value of a number in a context where
we don't know the type. In that case, the syntax of the number tells us
its type, and we use Go rules to resolve. Note there is no such thing as
a uint ideal constant in this situation - the value must be of int type.

nodes.Name: evalFieldChain
nodes.DocComment:
evalFieldChain evaluates .X.Y.Z possibly followed by arguments.
dot is the environment in which to evaluate arguments, while
receiver is the value being walked along the chain.

nodes.Name: evalField
nodes.DocComment:
evalField evaluates an expression like (.Field) or (.Field arg1 arg2).
The 'final' argument represents the return value from the preceding
value of the pipeline, if any.

nodes.Name: evalCall
nodes.DocComment:
evalCall executes a function or method call. If it's a method, fun already has the receiver bound, so
it looks just like a function call. The arg list, if non-nil, includes (in the manner of the shell), arg[0]
as the function itself.

nodes.Name: canBeNil
nodes.DocComment: canBeNil reports whether an untyped nil can be assigned to the type. See reflect.Zero.

Children.Name: case
Children.RawSource: reflect.Chan, reflect.Func, reflect.Interface, reflect.Map, reflect.Pointer, reflect.Slice

nodes.Name: validateType
nodes.DocComment: validateType guarantees that the value is valid and assignable to the type.

Children.Name: case
Children.RawSource: reflect.Uint, reflect.Uint8, reflect.Uint16, reflect.Uint32, reflect.Uint64, reflect.Uintptr

nodes.Name: indirect
nodes.DocComment:
indirect returns the item at the end of indirection, and a bool to indicate
if it's nil. If the returned bool is true, the returned value's kind will be
either a pointer or interface.

nodes.Name: indirectInterface
nodes.DocComment:
indirectInterface returns the concrete value in an interface value,
or else the zero reflect.Value.
That is, if v represents the interface value x, the result is the same as reflect.ValueOf(x):
the fact that x was an interface value is forgotten.

nodes.Name: printValue
nodes.DocComment:
printValue writes the textual representation of the value to the output of
the template.

nodes.Name: printableValue
nodes.DocComment:
printableValue returns the, possibly indirected, interface value inside v that
is best for a call to formatted printer.
